build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player ship scrolls horizontally through a side-view space environment, moving freely within screen bounds while the background auto-scrolls. Score 0 if there is no scrolling or the ship is static.

The ship fires projectiles that travel forward and destroy enemies on contact, with visible hit feedback such as explosions or flash effects. Score 0 if the ship cannot fire or projectiles have no effect.
Collecting power-up items upgrades the weapon through at least 3 visible tiers (e.g., single shot to spread to laser), and dying resets the chain. Score 0 if no power-up system exists.
A bomb or screen-clear ability destroys all on-screen enemy projectiles and damages enemies, with a limited stock shown in the HUD. Score 0 if no bomb mechanic exists.
The player has a lives system with visible life counter; losing all lives offers limited continues before game over. Score 0 if there is no life system or the player has infinite health.
At least 5 distinct stages are present with different background themes, enemy compositions, and scrolling patterns. Score 0 if only one stage exists or stages are visually identical.
At least 4 distinct enemy types with different movement patterns, firing behaviors, and visual designs appear across stages. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists.
Each stage ends with a multi-phase boss that has distinct attack patterns per phase and visible health or damage states. Score 0 if no bosses exist.
Power-up chain offers at least 3 weapon tiers with visually and functionally distinct firing patterns (spread, laser, homing, etc.). Score 0 if only one weapon exists.
A score system tracks performance with stage-end tallies and a final victory or game-over summary showing total score, lives used, and stages cleared. Score 0 if no scoring exists.

Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, a Start control, and space-themed imagery such as stars, ships, or nebulae. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to stage gameplay to boss encounter to stage-clear interstitial without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing or broken.
The HUD clearly shows score, lives, bomb stock, current weapon tier, and stage progress in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine game state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: firing shows muzzle flash, hits show explosions, power-up collection flashes, death triggers an animation, and boss phase changes are visually signaled. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, gameplay, bosses, HUD, and interstitials with a consistent space-themed palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
The player ship, enemies, bosses, projectiles, and power-ups use real sprite art with distinct silhouettes and animations. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled rectangles.

Animation brings the scene to life: scrolling parallax backgrounds, enemy movement animations, explosion sequences, boss phase transitions, and weapon firing effects. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with icons, framed panels, or custom fonts rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
